Subject: Sandbox compatibility & validation: Redwood + Stratus Plugins

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for taking a look. As discussed last week, Stratus Plugins is preparing a small certification pass against Redwood's hosted sandbox to validate feature parity for our inference plugin set (streamed responses, batched multi-request, and an embedders sidecar).

Attached is our test matrix (stratus-test-matrix.csv) and a short network checklist. High-level asks:
- Confirm streaming semantics across model variants (esp. causal vs encoder-decoder).
- Validate KV cache behavior when clients perform warm-up followed by a large burst.
- Confirm that the embedders sidecar (batched up to N=128 vectors) meets latency SLOs under reserved capacity.

We can be flexible on times — would like to schedule a 30–45m kick-off with your engineering and product leads. We can also drop a small set of sample payloads if that helps.

Attached: stratus-test-matrix.csv, network-checklist.pdf

Cheers,
Elliot Barnes
Head of Integrations
Stratus Plugins

On Tue, Jul 25, 2028 at 10:05 AM Grace O'Connor wrote:
> I've provisioned a temporary sandbox project for Stratus: sandbox-stratus-202807.

Quick tech notes from the runtime team before kickoff:
- Model variants: we'll run the tests against rdx-gpt-small-causal and rdx-gpt-med-encoder-decoder. Expect different streaming frame boundaries for the encoder-decoder family; we'll document the chunking behavior.
- Batching: default batch window is 12ms on the sandbox GPUs; we'll allow up to 200ms for experimental runs to maximize throughput.
- KV cache warm-up: if Stratus clients send a 256-token warm-up with repeated prefixes, KV hit rate should exceed 92% for subsequent requests — plan tests accordingly.
- Embedders sidecar: support for batched vectors up to 128; we'll test p99 latency for N=32,64,128 under 1, 3, 5 replica counts.
- Quantization paths: sandbox uses dynamic 4bit quant profiles; we expect slightly longer init times for the first request.

I'll bring a runbook to the kickoff and a simple JMeter script to reproduce bursts.

Sergio
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Elliot Barnes <elliot@stratusplugins.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@stratusplugins.io>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 16:50:00 -0700
Subject: FW: test run #4 results / stability snippet

Forwarding the quick run results we captured this morning (attached stability-log-snippet.txt). Key observations from our side:
- Streaming frames for the encoder-decoder model are chunked into uneven sizes when prompt contains long JSON payloads.
- One out of five runs showed an elevated tail latency during a cache-miss sequence (~1.8s p99).
- Embedder batch N=128 did hit our expected throughput, but latency spiked when combined with a simultaneous full-batch generation run.

We do have a small set of sanitized payloads attached as well; happy to run more experiments during your dry-run window.

Thanks,
Elliot

Thanks for the logs, Elliot. A few operational asks for the dry-run:
1) Deterministic pass: please run a deterministic pass with the same seed so we can rule out stochastic variance.
2) For the p99 cache-miss tail: capture a full trace (token timestamps) for the failing run and upload to the Drive link. Sergio — we'll need the kernel selection logs for that time window (sandbox keeps them for 72h).
3) Canary test config:
   - streaming: chunk size target = 512 bytes; max buffer latency = 40ms
   - generation: max tokens = 512, temp = 0.2, top_p = 0.95
   - embedder: batch N=64 (single replica) then scale to N=128 for stress test

If you can schedule the quiet-dry-run Thu morning (we'll coordinate on Slack #partner-sandbox), we'll collect the traces and reconvene Fri with initial pass/fail and a short remediation list.

Karthik

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sandbox compatibility & validation: Redwood + Stratus Plugins

Elliot/Samira — thanks for moving quickly on the artifacts and the runs. Quick summary and next steps:

What passed in dry-run:
- Embedders batched throughput at N=64 met our p95 latency target under single-replica load.
- Streaming semantics for causal models are consistent with our contract.

Open items (what we observed):
- Encoder-decoder streaming chunking inconsistency when payloads contain long embedded JSON (Sergio to capture kernel logs).
- Elevated p99 during explicit cache-miss bursts (we'll need the trace and kernel logs to correlate).
- Contention between embedder full-batch and concurrent generation spikes latency — recommended to separate heavy embedder runs to dedicated replica sets in production.

Next steps (action owners):
- Sergio: collect kernel selection logs for the p99 window and share by Thu 09:00 PT.
- Elliot: run deterministic pass with provided seed and upload token-timestamp traces to the Drive link by Thu 12:00 PT.
- Marissa: I'll loop product (APIs) on the encoder-decoder chunking behavior and capture any API contract mismatches.
- Karthik/Grace: schedule a remediation/retest early next week and confirm production deployment approach (dedicated embedder replicas).

I'll open a lightweight remediation ticket (HS-43827) and add the attachments from today's exchanges to the Drive folder. If we hit the acceptance criteria (no regression p99 > 1.5s on production-like runs), we'll provide a partner badge and list Stratus Plugins in our partner integrations catalog.

Thanks everyone for a productive week.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
